passage: At first glance, glass appears perfectly clear and orderly, yet at the molecular level it is composed of atoms arranged in complete disorder.
Scientists disagree on what to call this: some label it an amorphous solid, while others prefer the term supercooled liquid.
In theory, glass belongs to both categories, but in practice its behavior places it firmly in the solid camp.
Contrary to popular belief, the thicker bottoms of old stained-glass window panes are not caused by the glass slowly flowing downward over centuries.
Such unevenness simply reflects how those panes were originally shaped when they were first blown and cooled.
Flat, uniform sheets of glass were not achieved until the nineteenth century, with truly thin flat glass arriving even later.
Most strikingly, although glass is among humanity's oldest manufactured materials, the reason it behaves as it does remains unexplained.
As one craftsman memorably remarked, glass is not so much a material as it is a state of matter.
choices: the industrial applications of flat glass in modern architecture
the disordered molecular structure of glass and the mysteries it still poses to science
how medieval craftsmen perfected the art of making stained-glass windows
the chemical differences between amorphous solids and crystalline materials
why glass was the most important material invented in human history
theme.explanation_ko: 유리가 분자 수준에서 무정형이며 그 거동 원리가 과학적으로 미해결임을 다루는 글. '무정형 구조와 과학적 미스터리'인 ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①현대 건축 응용, ③스테인드글라스 제작 기술, ④무정형과 결정 차이의 화학, ⑤역사적 중요성은 글의 초점이 아니다.

passage: Glass looks clean and transparent, but zoom in to the molecular scale and it dissolves into a jumble of randomly placed atoms.
Scientists cannot even agree on a single name: is it an amorphous solid, or a supercooled liquid?
In practice, it acts like a solid at room temperature — it never flows, no matter how long you wait.
The thick lower edges of medieval stained-glass panes tell us nothing about glass flowing; they were simply made that way.
Flat glass had to be invented in the 1800s, and perfectly flat thin sheets did not arrive until a century later.
For all its long history stretching back thousands of years, glass still baffles the scientists who study it.
No one has yet produced a complete explanation of why glass does what it does at the molecular level.
A glassmaker put it best: glass is not a material — it is a state.
choices: Medieval Glass: A Window into Ancient Craftsmanship
Solid or Liquid? How Scientists Classify Glass
From Sand to Sheet: The Industrial History of Glass
Unsolved Mystery Behind the Nature of Glass
The Perfect Material: Why Glass Shaped Modern Civilization
title.explanation_ko: 유리가 가장 오래된 인공 물질 중 하나이지만 과학자들이 그 본성을 완전히 이해하지 못한다는 내용. '유리의 본질에 숨겨진 미해결 수수께끼'인 ④가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①중세 스테인드글라스 공예, ②분류 문제만 부각, ③산업적 역사, ⑤문명 기여도는 글의 핵심(미해결 수수께끼)과 다르다.

passage: Clear and perfect as it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms.
The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an amorphous solid, for others a supercooled liquid.
In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter.
Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time.
Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidifying in the first place.
Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass.
The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does.
As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.
grammar.explanation_ko: ④ they were blown and solidifying → 수동태 병렬 구조이므로 solidifying(현재분사)이 아니라 solidified(과거분사)가 되어야 한다. were blown and solidified가 올바른 수동태 병렬.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①양보의 도치 구문(adj. + as + S + V), ②분사 전치사 given, ③목적격 관계대명사 생략(you sometimes see), ⑤despite + 의미상 주어(it) + 동명사(being) — 모두 어법상 옳다.

passage: Clear and perfect as it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms.
The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an amorphous solid, for others a supercooled liquid.
In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter.
In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods of time.
Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time.
Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass.
The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to obscure why glass behaves the way it does.
Glass seems to follow most molecular laws.
As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.
vocab.explanation_ko: ⑤ struggle to obscure(모호하게 하려 애쓴다)는 과학자들이 유리의 거동 원인을 이해 못 한다는 문맥에 맞지 않는다 — comprehend(이해하다)가 올바른 어휘이다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①amorphous(무정형의), ②the latter(후자=고체), ③viscous(점성이 있는), ④misshapen(변형된)은 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

blank.distractor_ko: ②결과적으로, ③다행히도, ④마찬가지로, ⑤구체적으로는 앞 문장과의 역설적 대비를 나타내지 못한다.

passage: At the molecular level, glass is a disordered arrangement of atoms that can be called either an amorphous solid or a supercooled liquid.
In practice, glass never flows or behaves as a liquid at room temperature.
The uneven thickness of old stained-glass windows reflects original manufacturing methods, not slow flow over time.
Truly flat glass was only achieved in the twentieth century.
Despite glass being one of humanity's most ancient manufactured materials, scientists still cannot fully explain its molecular behavior.
Glass occupies a unique category — it is not simply a material but a state of matter.
This enduring puzzle shows that familiarity does not guarantee scientific understanding.
As one glassmaker captured it, glass defies easy classification.
summary.summary_template: Glass has a uniquely __(A)__ molecular structure that places it between a solid and a liquid, and despite its long history, scientists still __(B)__ to explain why it behaves the way it does.
summary.explanation_ko: 유리는 무작위 원자 배열로 '무질서한(disordered)' 구조이고, 과학자들은 여전히 이유를 '이해하려 애쓴다(struggle)'. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A) crystalline(결정형)은 본문과 정반대, simple(단순한)도 틀림. (B) refuse(거부하다), pretend(~인 척하다)는 의미상 맞지 않는다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 역설은, 유리가 가장 오래된 인간이 만든 물질 중 하나임에도 불구하고, 과학자들이 유리가 왜 그렇게 행동하는지 여전히 이해하려고 애쓴다는 것이다.
writing.answer: The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does.
writing.explanation_ko: The paradox is that + 명사절. despite + 의미상 주어(it) + 동명사(being). struggle to comprehend + 간접의문문(why glass behaves the way it does).

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 우리 눈에는 맑고 완벽해 보일지 모르지만, 분자 수준에서 내려다보면, 유리는 원자들이 무작위로 뒤섞인 공 풀장처럼 보인다.
writing.answer: Clear and perfect as it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms.
writing.explanation_ko: 형용사 도치 양보 구문: adj. + as + S + V = 'Although S + V + adj.' down at the molecular level(분자 수준에서). look like + 명사구.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이론적으로 유리는 액체이자 고체 모두이지만, 실제 거동 방식을 고려하면 실용적으로는 정말 후자에 가깝다.
conditions: In theory와 in practice를 각각 사용할 것
writing.answer: In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter.
writing.explanation_ko: In theory ... in practice 대비 구조. given the way it behaves(실제 거동 방식을 고려하면) 삽입구. the latter = solid(후자).

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time.
writing.answer: 오래된 스테인드글라스 창문에서 가끔 볼 수 있는, 위보다 아래쪽이 더 두꺼운 변형된 유리 판들은, 유리가 시간이 지나면서 서서히 가라앉고 있기 때문에 그런 모양이 된 것이 일반적으로 아니다.
writing.explanation_ko: misshapen(변형된), (목적격 관계사 생략) sheets you see(볼 수 있는 유리판), thicker at the bottom than the top(위보다 아래쪽이 더 두꺼운), slowly sinking over time(시간이 지나면서 서서히 가라앉는).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Glass has a uniquely (A)___________ molecular structure, and despite being one of humanity's oldest manufactured materials, scientists still (B)___________ to comprehend why it behaves as it does.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 유리는 원자들이 무작위로 배열된 '무질서한(disordered)' 분자 구조를 가짐. (B) 과학자들이 유리 거동 원인을 '이해하려 애쓴다(struggle)'는 본문 표현(struggle to comprehend)에서.

writing.question: 다음 글의 주제를 <조건>에 맞게 한 문장의 영어로 서술하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 유리의 분자 구조와 과학적 미스터리에 관한 글의 주제를 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.answer: Despite centuries of use, glass remains a scientific mystery because its disordered molecular nature is not yet fully understood.
writing.explanation_ko: 유리는 오래 사용되어 왔음에도(despite centuries of use), 무정형 분자 구조로 인해 과학자들이 완전히 이해하지 못하는 미스터리라는 글의 핵심을 담은 문장.
